title: Quantum correlations beat any local model
caption: For the singlet state the correlation between measurements at angle θ apart is E(θ) = −cos θ. A simple local hidden-variable model gives a straight line. At 45° the quantum correlation is -0.707 against −0.5, and four such settings give S = 4/√2 = 2√2 ≈ 2.83, beyond the local limit of 2.
alt: Correlation against the angle between analysers: the quantum curve minus cosine theta lies further from zero than the straight local-model line at 45 and 135 degrees.
description: A local model with hidden variables: E(θ) = −1 + 2θ/180°.
CHSH: S = |E(a,b) − E(a,b′) + E(a′,b) + E(a′,b′)| = 2√2 for the best angles; any local model gives at most 2.

checks.name: quantum correlation stronger than the local model at 45°
